12561.l: Lymantria dispar, also known as the gypsy moth, and in the United States, the spongy moth, is a species of moth in the family Erebidae native to Europe and Asia. Lymantria dispar is subdivided into several subspecies, with subspecies such as L. d. dispar and L. d. japonica being clearly identifiable without ambiguity. Lymantria dispar has been introduced to several continents and is now additionally found as an invasive species in Africa, North America and South America. The polyphagous larvae live on a variety of deciduous and coniferous trees and can cause severe damage in years of mass reproduction.

12806.l: Dasychira moerens is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Felder in 1894. It is found in South India and Sri Lanka.

12807.l: Dasychira obliquata, the streaked tussock moth, is a species of tussock moth in the family Erebidae. It is found in North America.

12808.l: Dasychira pinicola, the pine tussock moth, is a species of moth in the family Erebidae. It was first described by Harrison Gray Dyar Jr. in 1911 and is found in the eastern US.

12809.l: Dasychira plagiata, the northern pine tussock or northern conifer tussock, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Francis Walker in 1865. It is found in North America from Newfoundland and Labrador to Alberta, in Massachusetts, New York and North Carolina.

12810.l: Dasychira styx is a species of erebid moths in the subfamily Lymantriinae. It was described by George Thomas Bethune-Baker in 1911. Its type locality is in Angola.

12811.l: Dasychira tephra, the tephra tussock moth, is a tussock moth in the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Jacob Hübner in 1809. It is found in North America.

12812.l: Dasychira thwaitesi is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Frederic Moore in 1883. It is found in India and Sri Lanka.

12813.l: Dasychira vagans, the variable tussock moth, is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in North America, where it has been recorded from Newfoundland to southern British Columbia in the north and North Carolina and Utah in the west. The species was first described by William Barnes and James Halliday McDunnough in 1913.

12814.l: Calliteara is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Arthur Gardiner Butler in 1881.

12815.l: Calliteara abietis is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is found from northern and central Europe, through Russia to Japan.

12816.l: Calliteara albibasalis is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by William Jacob Holland in 1893. It is found in Gabon.

12817.l: Calliteara arizana is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Alfred Ernest Wileman in 1910. It is found in Taiwan.

12818.l: Calliteara baibarana is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Shōnen Matsumura in 1927. It is found in Taiwan.

12819.l: Calliteara farenoides is a species of moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in Queensland.

12820.l: Calliteara flavobrunnea is a moth of the family Erebidae. It was described by Robinson in 1969. It is found on Fiji.

12821.l: Calliteara fortunata is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Alois Friedrich Rogenhofer in 1891. It is found on the Canary Islands.

12822.l: Calliteara grotei is a species of moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in Asia in the Himalayas, southwestern India and in Southeast Asia.

12823.l: Calliteara horsfieldii, or Horsfield's tussock moth, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by the British entomologist Edward Saunders in 1851, and named in honor of the British naturalist Thomas Horsfield, who traveled southern Asia and published works on zoology from the region. C. horsfieldii can be found in southern Asia, the islands of the northern Indian Ocean, and many parts of south east Asia and Indonesia. It is also sometimes referred to as the Yellow Tussock Moth.

12824.l: Calliteara kikuchii is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Shōnen Matsumura in 1927. It is found in Taiwan.

12825.l: Calliteara lunulata is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in the Russian Far East, Japan, China and Taiwan.

12826.l: Calliteara nandarivatu is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae. It was described by Robinson in 1968. It is found on Fiji.

12827.l: Calliteara pudibunda, the pale tussock, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The Dutch common name for the moth (Meriansborstel) comes from the butterfly and insect painter Maria Sibylla Merian. The species was first described by Carl Linnaeus in his 1758 10th edition of Systema Naturae. It is found in Asia and Europe.

12828.l: Calliteara strigata is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Frederic Moore in 1879.

12829.l: Orgyia is a genus of tussock moths of the family Erebidae. The genus was described by Ochsenheimer in 1810. The species are cosmopolitan, except for the Neotropical realm.

12830.l: Orgyia leucostigma, the white-marked tussock moth, is a moth in the family Erebidae. The species was first described by James Edward Smith in 1797. The caterpillar is very common especially in late summer in eastern North America, extending as far west as Texas, California, and Alberta.

12831.l: Orgyia leucostigma sablensis is a subspecies of Orgyia leucostigma, the white-marked tussock moth, found only on Sable Island in Nova Scotia, Canada. The subspecies was first described by Kenneth Neil in 1979.

12832.l: Orgyia antiqua, the rusty tussock moth or vapourer, is a moth in the family Erebidae.

12833.l: Orgyia definita, the definite tussock moth or definite-marked tussock moth, is a moth of the family Erebidae. It was first described by Alpheus Spring Packard in 1865. The species is found in eastern North America from Minnesota to New Brunswick and south to South Carolina, Mississippi, and Louisiana.

12834.l: Orgyia detrita, the fir tussock moth or live oak tussock moth, is a tussock moth in the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Félix Édouard Guérin-Méneville in 1831. It is found in North America.

12835.l: Orgyia falcata is a species of tussock moth in the family Erebidae. It is found in North America.

12836.l: Orgyia leuschneri, the box-elder tussock moth, is a species of tussock moth in the family Erebidae. It is found in North America.

12837.l: Orgyia magna is a species of tussock moth in the family Erebidae. It is found in North America.

12838.l: Orgyia postica, the cocoa tussock moth or hevea tussock moth, is a species of moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae of the family Erebidae found in the Oriental tropics of India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Borneo, Java, New Guinea, and Taiwan. It was described by Francis Walker in 1855.

12839.l: Orgyia pseudotsugata, the Douglas-fir tussock moth, is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by James Halliday McDunnough in 1921. It is found in western North America. Its population periodically irrupts in cyclical outbreaks. The caterpillars feed on the needles of Douglas fir, true fir, and spruce in summer, and moths are on the wing from July or August to November.

12840.l: Orgyia thyellina, the white-spotted tussock moth, is a species of moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Arthur Gardiner Butler in 1881..

12841.l: Orgyia vetusta, also known as the western tussock moth, formerly Hemerocampa vetusta, is a moth found in the Pacific States and British Columbia. The species is dimorphic; the females are flightless.

12842.l: Orgyia viridescens is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in Sri Lanka.

12843.l: Laelia is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Stephens in 1828. Species are well distributed throughout Europe, Japan, China, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar and Java.

12844.l: Laelia cardinalis is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by George Hampson in 1893. It is found in Sri Lanka.

12845.l: Laelia coenosa, the reed tussock, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Jacob Hübner in 1808. It is found in North Africa, southern and central Europe, through Russia and eastern Asia up to Japan.

12846.l: Laelia exclamationis is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Vincenz Kollar in 1848. It is found in Sri Lanka, India and Taiwan.

12847.l: Laelia fasciata is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Frederic Moore in 1883. It is found in Sri Lanka, India and Myanmar. One subspecies is recognized, Laelia fasciata rubripennis Moore, 1884.

12848.l: Laelia fracta is a species of moth of the family Erebidae described by William Schaus and W. G. Clements in 1893.

12849.l: Laelia rosea is a species of moth of the family Erebidae. It was described by William Schaus and W. G. Clements in 1893 and is found in Sierra Leone.

12850.l: Laelia striata is a species of moth of the family Erebidae first described by Alfred Ernest Wileman in 1910. It is found in Taiwan.

12851.l: Laelia suffusa is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by George Hampson in 1893. It is found in Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Java, East Indies, Sundaland, the Philippines and Sulawesi.

12852.l: Laelia testacea is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in India and Sri Lanka.

12853.l: Aroa is a genus of moths in the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. Species are distributed in South Africa, China, throughout India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, and Java.

12854.l: Aroa danva is a moth in the subfamily Lymantriinae described by William Schaus and W. G. Clements in 1893.

12855.l: Aroa major is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by George Hampson in 1893. It is found in Sri Lanka.

12856.l: Aroa maxima is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by George Hampson in 1893. It is found in Sri Lanka.

12857.l: Aroa plana is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in India and Sri Lanka. The caterpillar is known to feed on Bambusa species.

12858.l: Aroa sienna is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by George Hampson in 1891. It is found in India (Nilgiri) and Sri Lanka.

12859.l: Aroa subnotata is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in Sri Lanka.

12860.l: Aroa yokoae is a moth in the family Erebidae. It was described by George Thomas Bethune-Baker in 1927. It is found in Cameroon.

12861.l: Mpanjaka is a genus of moths in the subfamily Lymantriinae. The genus was erected by Paul Griveaud in 1976.

12862.l: Mpanjaka albovirida is a moth of the family of Erebidae that is found in North Madagascar.

12863.l: Mpanjaka betschi is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Paul Griveaud in 1974. It is found in central Madagascar.

12867.l: Mpanjaka montana is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Paul Griveaud in 1974. It is found in central Madagascar.

12868.l: Mpanjaka pastor is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Arthur Gardiner Butler in 1882. It is found in central Madagascar.

12869.l: Gynaephora is a genus of "tussock moths", also known as the Lymantriinae, within the family Erebidae. They are mainly found in the Holarctic in alpine, Arctic and Subarctic regions, and are best known for their unusually long larval development period. The life-cycle of Gynaephora groenlandica was once believed to take fourteen years, but subsequent studies reduced it to seven, still a very slow development rate that is extremely rare in the Lepidoptera. The caterpillars have five instars, with each instar lasting a year.

12870.l: Gynaephora groenlandica, the Arctic woolly bear moth, is an erebid moth native to the High Arctic in the Canadian archipelago, Greenland and Wrangel Island in Russia. It is known for its slow rate of development, as its full caterpillar life cycle may extend up to 7 years, with moulting occurring each spring. This species remains in a larval state for the vast majority of its life. Rare among Lepidoptera, it undergoes an annual period of diapause that lasts for much of the calendar year, as G. groenlandica is subject to some of the longest, most extreme winters on Earth. 12871.l: Gynaephora rossii, in English known as Ross' tussock moth, is a species of tussock moth in the family Erebidae. It is widespread in the tundras and highlands of the Holarctic. It has large, furry caterpillars which seem to eat mostly saxifrages.

12872.l: Gynaephora selenitica is a moth in the family Erebidae first described by Eugenius Johann Christoph Esper in 1789. It is found from central Europe through eastern Europe to the Urals and Ob' River in West Siberia. It is not found in western and southern Europe and Scandinavia.

12873.l: Clethrogyna is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was described by Rambur in 1866.

12874.l: Clethrogyna antiquoides is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in most of Europe, the Ural, Armenia, Mongolia, and China. This species has commonly been placed in the genus Orgyia but molecular analyses support the genus Clethrogyna as a separate lineage.

12875.l: Clethrogyna aurolimbata is a species of moth of the family Erebidae first described by Achille Guenée in 1835. It is found in the Pyrenees and on the Iberian Peninsula. The larvae feed on Genista species, including Genista purgans. This species has commonly been placed in the genus Orgyia but molecular analyses support the genus Clethrogyna as a separate lineage.

12876.l: Dicallomera is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae.

12877.l: Dicallomera fascelina, the dark tussock, is a moth in the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Carl Linnaeus in his 1758 10th edition of Systema Naturae. It is found in most of Europe, through the Palearctic to Central Asia to Korea.

12878.l: Dicallomera pumila is a little seen species of moth of the family Erebidae found in mountains in Kazakhstan and in the southern Urals.

12879.l: Ilema is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was described by Walker in 1855 and renamed by Moore in 1860, because Walker's chosen name was preoccupied.

12880.l: Ilema kosemponica is a moth in the family Erebidae first described by Embrik Strand in 1914. It is found in Taiwan.

12881.l: Ilema virescens is a species of moth in the family Erebidae that was first described by Frederic Moore in 1879. It is found in India.

12882.l: Olene is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Jacob Hübner in 1823.

12883.l: Olene dudgeoni is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Charles Swinhoe in 1907. It is found from the north-eastern Himalayas to Indochina, Taiwan and Sundaland.

12884.l: Olene mendosa, the brown tussock moth or hairy tussock moth, is a species of moth in the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Jacob Hübner in 1823. It is found in India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Taiwan, Thailand and Australia.

12885.l: Penthophera is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Ernst Friedrich Germar in 1812.

12886.l: Penthophera lutea is an owlet moth species. It was first described by Jean Baptiste Boisduval in 1847. It is found in South Africa.

12887.l: Penthophera morio is a moth species of subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Carl Linnaeus in 1767.

12888.l: Teia is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855.

12889.l: The painted apple moth (Teia anartoides) is a tussock moth native to Australia. It is notable as a pest in pine forests, and is classified as a pest in New Zealand. Some sources still refer to this species as belonging to the genus Orgyia, but in 2015 the genus Teia was recognized as a separate lineage.

12890.l: Teia athlophora is a species of tussock moth found in southwestern Australia. The type specimen was collected from Perth, Western Australia.

12891.l: Acyphas is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae erected by Jacob Hübner in 1819.

12892.l: Acyphas semiochrea, the omnivorous tussock moth, is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Gottlieb August Wilhelm Herrich-Schäffer in 1855. It is found along most of the coast of Australia, including: New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria and Western Australia.

12893.l: Belinda is a monotypic moth genus in the subfamily Lymantriinae. Its only species, Belinda zoe, is found in Indonesia. Both the genus and species were first described by Alexander Schintlmeister and Thomas J. Witt in 2014.

12894.l: Belinda is a monotypic moth genus in the subfamily Lymantriinae. Its only species, Belinda zoe, is found in Indonesia. Both the genus and species were first described by Alexander Schintlmeister and Thomas J. Witt in 2014.

12896.l: Casama vilis is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1865. It is found in Sri Lanka, India, Middle East, Ethiopia, Kenya and Somalia.

12897.l: Eudasychira is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae.

12898.l: Eudasychira ampliata is a tussock moth from Madagascar, first described by Arthur Gardiner Butler in 1878, and formerly placed in its own genus, Vietteria.

12899.l: Griveaudyria is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae.

12900.l: Griveaudyria mascarena is a tussock moth from Madagascar, first described by Arthur Gardiner Butler in 1878.

12902.l: Ocneria detrita is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae. The species was first described by Eugenius Johann Christoph Esper in 1785. It is found in France, Italy and parts of central, south-east and eastern Europe.

12903.l: Psalis is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was described by Jacob Hübner in 1823.

12904.l: Psalis pennatula, the yellow hairy caterpillar, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Johan Christian Fabricius in 1793. It is found in India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Australia and Java.

12905.l: Telochurus is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae erected by Koen V. N. Maes in 1984.

12906.l: Telochurus recens, the scarce vapourer, is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae found in Europe. The species was first described by Jacob Hübner in 1819. The wingspan is for the males; the females are wingless. The moth flies from June to July depending on the location. The larvae feed on various deciduous trees, such as Crataegus and Salix species. This species has commonly been placed in the genus Orgyia but molecular analyses support its exclusion from that genus, and placement in the genus Telochurus.

12907.l: Cifuna is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1855.

12908.l: Habrophylla is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was described by Alfred Jefferis Turner in 1921. All the species are found in Australia.

12909.l: Neomardara is a genus of moths in the subfamily Lymantriinae. The genus was described by Hering in 1926.

12910.l: Pantana is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1855.

12911.l: The Nygmiini are a tribe of tussock moths of the Erebidae family. ==Description== Adult females of the tribe have an enlarged seventh abdominal segment with a tuft of scales and use this adaptation to protect their egg mass.

12912.l: Euproctis is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae described by Jacob Hübner in 1819. Species are cosmopolitan, widespread throughout Palearctic, African, Oriental and Australian regions. Molecular phylogenetic studies indicate that the genus as presently understood comprises a large number of unrelated lineages (i.e., is paraphyletic), only a few of which have names (e.g., the genera Kidokuga and Sphrageidus), and is therefore in serious need of revision.

12913.l: Euproctis annulipes is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in La Réunion.

12914.l: Euproctis apoblepta is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in Madagascar.

12915.l: Euproctis baliolalis, the browntail gum moth, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Charles Swinhoe in 1892. It is found in the south-east quarter of Australia.

12916.l: Euproctis bimaculata is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in India, Sri Lanka and Thailand.

12917.l: Euproctis cervina is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Frederic Moore in 1877. It is found in Sri Lanka.

12918.l: The brown-tail moth (Euproctis chrysorrhoea) is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is native to Europe, neighboring countries in Asia, and the north coast of Africa. Descriptions of outbreaks, i.e., large population increases of several years duration, have been reported as far back as the 1500s. The life cycle of the moth is atypical, in that it spends approximately nine months (August to April) as larvae (caterpillars), leaving about one month each for pupae, imagos and eggs. Larvae (caterpillars) are covered in hairs. Two red spots on the back, toward the tail, distinguish these species from other similarly hairy moth larvae.

12919.l: Euproctis flavinata is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1865. It is found in China and Hong Kong.

12920.l: Euproctis fraterna is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Frederic Moore in 1883. It is found in the Maldives, India, Sri Lanka and the Seychelles.

12921.l: Euproctis fulvipuncta is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by George Hampson in 1893. It is found in India and Sri Lanka.

12922.l: Euproctis insulata (Chinese:, Yellow-Spotted Poisonous Moth) is a moth in the family Erebidae first described by Alfred Ernest Wileman in 1910. It is found in Taiwan.

12923.l: Euproctis kanshireia is a moth in the family Erebidae. It is found in Taiwan.

12924.l: Euproctis latifascia is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in India, Sri Lanka and Taiwan.

12925.l: Euproctis limbalis, the bordered browntail moth, is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Gottlieb August Wilhelm Herrich-Schäffer in 1855. It is known from Australia, including Queensland and New South Wales.

12926.l: Euproctis lunata, the castor hairy caterpillar, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Thailand.

12927.l: Euproctis lutea, the fresh-water mangrove itchy caterpillar, is a species of moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in northern Australia (the Northern Territory, Queensland and New South Wales) and New Guinea.

12928.l: Euproctis marginalis, the margined browntail moth, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in Australia, including Tasmania.

12929.l: Euproctis mayottensis is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Cyril Leslie Collenette in 1956. It is found in Mayotte.

12930.l: Euproctis melanosoma is a species of moth of the family Erebidae. It is known from New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania and Victoria.

12931.l: Euproctis pulverea is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by John Henry Leech in 1888. It is found in Japan, Korea and Taiwan.

12932.l: Euproctis purpureofasciata is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in Taiwan.

12933.l: Euproctis rhoda is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Frederic Moore in 1879. It is sometimes classified as a subspecies of Euproctis howra. It is found in India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, the Andaman Islands and Australia.

12934.l: Euproctis semisignata is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1865. It is found in India and Sri Lanka.

12935.l: The yellow-tail, goldtail moth or swan moth (Sphrageidus similis) is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Johann Kaspar Füssli in 1775, and has commonly been placed within the related genus Euproctis. It is distributed throughout Europe to the Urals, then east across the Palearctic to Siberia and south to India and Sri Lanka.

12936.l: Euproctis taiwana, the Taiwan yellow tussock moth, is a species of tussock moth in the family Erebidae.

12937.l: Euproctis varians is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Celebes and China.

12938.l: Euproctis virguncula is a species of moth in the family Erebidae. It is a pest of millets.

12939.l: Nygmia is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Jacob Hübner in 1820.

12940.l: Nygmia amplior is a species of moth in the family Erebidae. It is a pest of millets in India.

12941.l: Nygmia icilia is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Caspar Stoll in 1790. It is found in India and Sri Lanka.

12942.sd: Species of moth found in Asia
12942.l: Nygmia plana is a moth in the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1856. It has been spotted in India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, China, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines and Japan.

12943.l: Nygmia semifumosa is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is endemic to Borneo. Males have a characteristically sparse and irregular scattering of black scales on the yellow forewing. Females have a similar, but even more sparse scattering, and diagnostic white patches; the hindwings are dark grey to about two thirds.

12944.l: Nygmia solitaria is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo.

12945.l: Nygmia xanthomela is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1862. It is found in Sri Lanka, Borneo, Java, Sumatra and Peninsular Malaysia.

12946.l: Artaxa is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae erected by Francis Walker in 1855. Some of the species have urticating hairs.

12947.l: Artaxa angulata is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Shōnen Matsumura in 1927. It is found in Taiwan, Myanmar, India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia.

12948.l: Artaxa digramma is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Jean Baptiste Boisduval in 1844. It is found in India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Nepal, Java, Borneo, and recently China.

12949.l: Artaxa drucei is a species of moth in the genus Artaxa found in Papua New Guinea. There are 13 collected specimens, all at the Smithsonian Institution's National Museum of Natural History.

12950.l: Artaxa guttata is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and India.

12951.l: Artaxa vitellina is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Vincenz Kollar in 1848. It is found in India and Sri Lanka.

12952.l: Somena is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1856.

12953.l: Somena aurantiacoides is a moth in the family Erebidae. It was described by Jeremy Daniel Holloway in 1999. It is found on Borneo and Sumatra.

12954.l: Somena exigua is a moth in the family Erebidae. It was described by John Nietner in 1861. It is found in Sri Lanka.

12955.l: Somena moorei is a moth in the family Erebidae. It was described by Pieter Cornelius Tobias Snellen in 1879. It is found on Sulawesi.

12956.l: Somena scintillans, the yellow tail tussock moth, is a moth in the family Erebidae described by Francis Walker in 1856. It is found in northern India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar and the Andaman Islands. Though considered a minor pest, larva can sporadically be a serious pest.

12957.l: Somena similis is a moth in the family Erebidae. It was described by Frederic Moore in 1860. It is found from India to Sundaland.

12958.l: Arna is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1855. It contains many species formerly included in the genus Euproctis, such as Arna bipunctapex.

12959.l: Arna apicalis is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1865. It is found in Sri Lanka.

12960.l: Arna bipunctapex is a species of moth in the family Erebidae. It is found from India to Indochina and in Taiwan and Sundaland.

12961.l: Arna micronides is a species of moth in the family Erebidae. It is a pest of millets in India.

12962.l: Arna pseudoconspersa, the tea tussock moth or Japanese browntail moth, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Embrik Strand in 1914. It is found in Japan, Taiwan, Korea, China, Vietnam and India.

12963.l: Toxoproctis is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Jeremy Daniel Holloway in 1999.

12964.l: Toxoproctis cosmia is a moth of the family Erebidae. It is found in Sundaland.

12965.l: Toxoproctis croceola is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Embrik Strand in 1918. It is found in Taiwan and China.

12966.l: Walker circumscribed the genus in 1865 with his newly-described B. apicalis as its sole member.

12967.l: Bembina apicalis is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1865. It is found in India and Sri Lanka.

12968.l: Epeuproctis is a monotypic moth genus in the family Erebidae. Its only species, Epeuproctis tamahonis, is found in Taiwan. Both the genus and species were first described by Shōnen Matsumura, the genus in 1933 and the species in 1927.

12969.l: Epeuproctis is a monotypic moth genus in the family Erebidae. Its only species, Epeuproctis tamahonis, is found in Taiwan. Both the genus and species were first described by Shōnen Matsumura, the genus in 1933 and the species in 1927.

12970.l: Lacida is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1855.

12971.l: Lacida costalis is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in Sri Lanka.

12972.l: Medama is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Shōnen Matsumura in 1933.

12973.l: Medama diplaga is a moth in the family Erebidae first described by George Hampson in 1910. It is found in Taiwan and India.

12974.l: Orvasca is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1865.

12975.l: Orvasca subnotata is a nygmiine tussock moth in the family Erebidae, found in Indomalaya and East Asia, where it is known as a pest that feeds on millets. The species was first described by Francis Walker in 1865.

12976.l: Sphrageidus is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. It is considered a synonym of the related genus Euproctis by some authors, but still recognized as valid by others (e.g.), and supported as distinct in molecular phylogenetic studies.

12977.l: Sphrageidus xanthorrhoea is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Vincenz Kollar in 1848. It is found in India, Sri Lanka, Java and Indonesia. It was once classified under the genus Euproctis, where it is accepted by some authors.

12978.l: Albarracina is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae.

12979.l: Choerotricha is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was described by Felder in 1874.

12980.l: Cozola is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1865.

12981.l: Kidokuga is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Yasunori Kishida in 2010. It is considered a synonym of the related genus Euproctis by some authors, but recognized as valid by others (e.g.), and supported as distinct in molecular phylogenetic studies.

12982.l: Micromorphe is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Felder in 1874.

12983.l: Rhypotoses is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Cyril Leslie Collenette in 1931.

12984.l: Sundaroa is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Jeremy Daniel Holloway in 1999.

12985.l: The Locharnini are a tribe of tussock moths of the family Erebidae. The tribe was erected by Jeremy Daniel Holloway and Houshuai Wang in 2015.

12986.l: Eloria is a genus of moths in the subfamily Lymantriinae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1855.

12987.l: Eloria diaphana is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Stoll in 1781. It is found in Suriname.

12988.l: Eloria noyesi, the coca tussock moth, is a moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by William Schaus in 1927. It is beige and its larvae feed on coca plants. It is found mostly in Peru and Colombia. The government of Colombia has proposed a plan to release large numbers of these moths to destroy the coca crops in their country.

12989.l: Numenes is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1855.

12990.l: Numenes siletti is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Francis Walker in 1855. It is found in north-eastern India and Peninsular Malaysia.

12991.l: Numenes takamukui is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Shōnen Matsumura in 1927. It is found in Taiwan.

12992.l: Pida is a genus of moths in the subfamily Lymantriinae. The genus was erected by Francis Walker in 1865, and including members of the former genus Ramadra.

12993.l: Pida patrana is a moth of the family Erebidae first described by Frederic Moore in 1859. It is found in north-eastern Bhutan, India (Bengal), Nepal and Taiwan.

12994.l: Pida postalba is a species of moth of the subfamily Lymantriinae first described by Wileman in 1910. It is found in Taiwan.

12995.l: Locharna is a genus of tussock moths in the family Erebidae. The genus was erected by Frederic Moore in 1879.

12996.l: Locharna strigipennis is a moth in the family Erebidae first described by Frederic Moore in 1879. It is found in the north-eastern Himalaya, India, China and Taiwan.

12997.l: Peloroses is a genus of moths in the family Erebidae. It is monotypic, being represented by the single species, Peloroses praestans.

12999.l: Euproctoides is a genus of moths in the subfamily Lymantriinae. The genus was erected by George Thomas Bethune-Baker in 1911.
